Chapter 4: Choosing Love as the Guiding Principle
With every new scroll, Hafid’s idea of what success really meant kept evolving. The next lesson? It sounds simple, but it’s anything but easy—choose love in everything you do.
Think about it. In a world that often praises aggression or cunning, leading with love can feel almost...naive, right? But as Hafid started living this out, he discovered something quietly powerful.
The scroll encouraged him to start each day with compassion, not just for himself, but for everyone he met. Instead of seeing other people as competition or obstacles, he began to see them as fellow travelers—each one carrying their own struggles, their own dreams.
In the marketplace, this shift was subtle, but the impact was huge. Hafid’s conversations warmed up. He grew more patient. Even the toughest customers seemed to soften in response.
One morning, a tired traveler wandered into the market—his clothes were torn, his eyes wary. Most merchants just looked past him, figuring he didn’t have a coin to his name. But Hafid remembered the scroll’s advice. He greeted the man with genuine kindness, listened to his story, even offered him a meal—no strings attached.
The traveler was so moved, he came back a few days later with friends, all eager to do business with someone who saw them as more than just a sale.
That’s when it really hit Hafid—love isn’t just a feeling, it’s a choice. It’s a new way of looking at people and situations. Most folks walk through life with their guard up, worried they’ll look weak or get taken advantage of. But when Hafid chose love first, he noticed doors opening that had always been shut. Trust started to grow, relationships got deeper, and opportunities popped up where he’d never seen them before.
The scroll’s wisdom went beyond just business. Hafid found that when he treated his own mistakes with compassion, he didn’t beat himself up—he just picked himself up and tried again. He forgave others more easily, too, realizing everyone’s just doing the best they can with what they’ve got.
Sure, there were moments when choosing love felt risky. Sometimes, people took advantage of his kindness. But Hafid discovered that those disappointments were rare—and the rewards, the trust and respect he gained, were worth it every time.
The real lesson? Love isn’t about big, dramatic gestures. It’s about all those small, daily choices: treating people with respect, listening without judging, helping out without expecting anything back. Over time, those choices became a habit. And that habit didn’t just change Hafid’s business—it changed his whole life.
